clinician.final_diagnosis: POLG-related mitochondrial cytopathy (biallelic compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in POLG: c.2243G>C p.Trp748Ser and c.3720G>C p.Arg1240His)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 21-year-old woman with no prior neurological history presented at 18 weeks gestation with focal impaired awareness seizures (right upper limb extension with twitching progressing to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures). She was afebrile with no preceding febrile illness. Seizures rapidly progressed to prolonged, refractory status epilepticus requiring ICU admission. EEG confirmed electroclinical status epilepticus. MR brain imaging revealed new abnormal cortical signal involving the left parietal, posterolateral temporal, and occipital lobes. CSF analysis showed normal white cell count, normal protein, no oligoclonal bands, and was negative for viral PCR and immune-mediated antibodies (anti-CASP2, NMDA, LGI1, GABA-B, AMPA 1/2, GAD, glycine), effectively ruling out infectious or autoimmune encephalitis. Seizure control was established with multiple anti-seizure medications (sodium valproate, phenobarbital, levetiracetam) and intravenous corticosteroids. The patient was transferred to a tertiary center and underwent late surgical termination of pregnancy at 23 weeks gestation per patient choice. Subsequent POLG genetic testing on blood detected biallelic compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in POLG (c.2243G>C p.Trp748Ser and c.3720G>C p.Arg1240His), confirming mitochondrial DNA polymerase deficiency as the underlying etiology. The seizures represent the initial manifestation of POLG-related mitochondrial cytopathy, unmasked or exacerbated by the metabolic stress of pregnancy.

MR brain imaging revealed new abnormal cortical signal involving the left parietal, posterolateral temporal, and occipital lobes. CSF analysis showed normal white cell count, normal protein, no oligoclonal bands, and was negative for viral PCR and immune-mediated antibodies (anti-CASP2, NMDA, LGI1, GABA-B, AMPA 1/2, GAD, glycine), effectively ruling out infectious or autoimmune encephalitis. Seizure control was established with multiple anti-seizure medications (sodium valproate, phenobarbital, levetiracetam) and intravenous corticosteroids. The patient was transferred to a tertiary center and underwent late surgical termination of pregnancy at 23 weeks gestation per patient choice. Subsequent POLG genetic testing on blood detected biallelic compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in POLG (c.2243G>C p.Trp748Ser and c.3720G>C p.Arg1240His), confirming mitochondrial DNA polymerase deficiency as the underlying etiology. The seizures represent the initial manifestation of POLG-related mitochondrial cytopathy, unmasked or exacerbated by the metabolic stress of pregnancy.

Seizures had focal semiology (right upper limb extension with twitching) progressing to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures
No preceding febrile illness and patient was afebrile on admission
No prior history of febrile seizures, meningitis, developmental delay, head injury, or birth complications
EEG confirmed electroclinical status epilepticus
MR brain scan showed new abnormal cortical signal involving the left parietal, posterolateral temporal and occipital lobes
CSF analysis showed normal white cell count, normal protein concentration, no oligoclonal bands, and was negative for viral PCR and immune-mediated antibodies
Seizures progressed to prolonged, refractory status epilepticus requiring ICU admission
Seizure control was established with multiple anti-seizure medications and intravenous corticosteroids
Patient was transferred to tertiary center and underwent late surgical termination of pregnancy at 23 weeks gestation
On arrival at tertiary center, patient was taking three anti-seizure medications (sodium valproate, phenobarbital, levetiracetam) and corticosteroids
